        if not want("swim", 1, math.clamp(speed / 10, 0.05, 4)) then want("walk", 1, 1) end
    elseif state == "swimidle" then
        if not want("swimidle", 1, 1) then want("idle", 1, 1) end
    elseif not want(state, 1, 1) then
        want("idle", 1, 1)
    end
    -- The idle look-around is picked again each time the character stops.
    if state ~= "idle" then puppet.Variant.idle = nil end
    if state ~= "sit" and entry.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Tool") then want("toolnone", 1, 1) end
    for _, row in pairs(wanted) do
        local track = Overlay.puppetTrack(entry, row[1], row[2])
        if track then
            pcall(function()
                if not track.IsPlaying then track:Play(0.15, row[3], row[4])
                else
                    if math.abs(track.WeightTarget - row[3]) > 0.02 then track:AdjustWeight(row[3], 0.15) end
                    if math.abs(track.Speed - row[4]) > 0.02 then track:AdjustSpeed(row[4]) end
                end
            end)
        end
    end
    for key, track in pairs(puppet.Tracks) do
        if track and not wanted[key] and track.IsPlaying then pcall(function() track:Stop(0.15) end) end
    end
end
-- FOLLOWING THE BODY on a puppet: games pose your character with animations of their own (a knife or a gun raised in
-- both hands, an item carried in front, an emote, a game move), and a puppet only plays walking and standing, so it
-- held them hanging down or stood still. While your character holds a tool or an item in a hand, or the game plays an
-- animation of its own on it, the puppet's arms follow your character's arms; while the game's animation plays, its
-- legs, torso and head follow too. An R6 limb is one piece, so it points where the R15 limb points (from its top to
-- the end of its lower part, the elbow or knee bend included); an R15 limb takes the R6 limb's turn at the shoulder or
-- hip and stays straight.
Overlay.Limbs = {
    {Key = "RightArm", Arm = true, R6 = {"Torso", "Right Arm"}, R15 = {"UpperTorso", "RightUpperArm", "RightLowerArm"}},
    {Key = "LeftArm", Arm = true, R6 = {"Torso", "Left Arm"}, R15 = {"UpperTorso", "LeftUpperArm", "LeftLowerArm"}},
    {Key = "RightLeg", R6 = {"Torso", "Right Leg"}, R15 = {"LowerTorso", "RightUpperLeg", "RightLowerLeg"}},
    {Key = "LeftLeg", R6 = {"Torso", "Left Leg"}, R15 = {"LowerTorso", "LeftUpperLeg", "LeftLowerLeg"}},
    {Key = "Head", R6 = {"Torso", "Head"}, R15 = {"UpperTorso", "Head"}},
    {Key = "Torso", R6 = {"HumanoidRootPart", "Torso"}, R15 = {"HumanoidRootPart", "LowerTorso"}},
}
-- The joint that moves a part of a model (not one inside a tool), with its parts and offsets.
function Overlay.jointTo(model, partName)
    for _, joint in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
        if (joint:IsA("Motor6D") or joint:IsA("AnimationConstraint")) and not joint:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Tool") then
            local ok, p0, p1, c0, c1 = pcall(Overlay.jointInfo, joint)
            if ok and p0 and p1 and c0 and c1 and p1.Name == partName and p1:IsDescendantOf(model) then return joint, p0, p1, c0, c1 end
        end
    end
    return nil
end
-- Each puppet joint with the real parts it follows (built once per link).
function Overlay.limbRig(entry)
    local target = entry.Target or entry.Character
    local own = F.getTrueRigType(entry.Model) == Enum.HumanoidRigType.R6 and "R6" or "R15"
    local real = F.getTrueRigType(target) == Enum.HumanoidRigType.R6 and "R6" or "R15"
    local found = entry.FoundParts or {}
    local function part(name)
        if name == "HumanoidRootPart" then return entry.RealRoot end
        return Overlay.pick(entry, found[name]) or target:FindFirstChild(name)
    end
    local limbs = {}
    for _, spec in ipairs(Overlay.Limbs) do
        local joint, _, _, c0 = Overlay.jointTo(entry.Model, spec[own][2])
        local names = spec[real]
        local limb = joint and {Joint = joint, Turn = c0 - c0.Position, Arm = spec.Arm == true}
        if limb and own == "R6" and real == "R15" and names[3] then
            -- An R6 limb points along the R15 limb, measured in the upper torso (which the R6 torso follows).
            limb.Ref, limb.Upper, limb.Lower = part("UpperTorso"), part(names[2]), part(names[3])
            if not (limb.Ref and limb.Upper and limb.Lower) then limb = nil end
        elseif limb then
            local b = (own == "R6" and real == "R15" and spec.Key == "Torso") and "UpperTorso" or names[2]
            limb.RealA, limb.RealB = part(names[1]), part(b)
            local _, realA, _, rc0, rc1 = Overlay.jointTo(target, b)
            local rest = (realA and realA == limb.RealA and rc0 and rc1) and rc0 * rc1:Inverse() or CFrame.new()
            limb.Rest = rest - rest.Position
            if not (limb.RealA and limb.RealB) then limb = nil end
        end
        if limb then table.insert(limbs, limb) end
    end
    entry.Limbs = limbs
end
-- What the game is doing with your character: holding something (a tool, an item in a hand), and whether it plays an
-- animation of its own (not Animate's).
function Overlay.posing(entry)
    local character = entry.Character
    local holding = character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Tool") ~= nil
    if not holding then
        for _, row in pairs(entry.Carried or {}) do
            local anchor = type(row) == "table" and row.Anchor
            if anchor and (anchor.Name:find("Hand$") or anchor.Name:find("Arm$")) then holding = true; break end
        end
    end
    local hum = character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    local animator = hum and hum:FindFirstChildOfClass("Animator")
    local animating = false
    if animator then
        local animate = character:FindFirstChild("Animate")
        for _, track in ipairs(animator:GetPlayingAnimationTracks()) do
            if track.WeightCurrent > 0.3 and not F.isAnimateTrack(track, animate) then animating = true; break end
        end
    end
    return holding or animating, animating
end
-- The shortest turn taking one direction to another.
function Overlay.arc(from, to)
    local dot = math.clamp(from:Dot(to), -1, 1)
    local axis = from:Cross(to)
    if axis.Magnitude < 1e-6 then return dot > 0 and CFrame.new() or CFrame.fromAxisAngle(Vector3.new(1, 0, 0), math.pi) end
    return CFrame.fromAxisAngle(axis.Unit, math.acos(dot))
end
-- The puppet joint's Transform for one limb: the turn the real limb has from its rest, in its parent part's axes, put
-- into the puppet joint's own axes. Nil when the real limb can't be read this frame.
function Overlay.limbTurn(limb)
    local delta
    if limb.Upper then
        local top = limb.Upper.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, limb.Upper.Size.Y / 2, 0)
        local bottom = limb.Lower.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, -limb.Lower.Size.Y / 2, 0)
        local direction = limb.Ref.CFrame:VectorToObjectSpace(bottom.Position - top.Position)
        if direction.Magnitude < 1e-4 then return nil end
        delta = Overlay.arc(Vector3.new(0, -1, 0), direction.Unit)
    else
        local relative = limb.RealA.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(limb.RealB.CFrame)
        delta = (relative - relative.Position) * limb.Rest:Inverse()
    end
    return limb.Turn:Inverse() * delta * limb.Turn
end
function Overlay.puppetLimbs(entry)
    local now = os.clock()
    local dt = math.clamp(now - (entry.LimbClock or now), 0, 0.1); entry.LimbClock = now
    local arms, body = Overlay.posing(entry)
    -- Eased in and out over a moment, so the limbs don't snap.
    entry.ArmBlend = math.clamp((entry.ArmBlend or 0) + (arms and dt or -dt) / 0.15, 0, 1)
    entry.BodyBlend = math.clamp((entry.BodyBlend or 0) + (body and dt or -dt) / 0.2, 0, 1)
    if entry.ArmBlend <= 0 and entry.BodyBlend <= 0 then return end
    if not entry.Limbs then Overlay.limbRig(entry) end
    for _, limb in ipairs(entry.Limbs) do
        local parts = limb.Upper and {limb.Ref, limb.Upper, limb.Lower} or {limb.RealA, limb.RealB}
        for _, item in ipairs(parts) do if not item.Parent then entry.Limbs = nil; return end end
        if not limb.Joint.Parent then entry.Limbs = nil; return end
        local blend = limb.Arm and math.max(entry.ArmBlend, entry.BodyBlend) or entry.BodyBlend
        if blend > 0 then
            local wanted = Overlay.limbTurn(limb)
            if wanted then limb.Joint.Transform = blend >= 1 and wanted or limb.Joint.Transform:Lerp(wanted, blend) end
        end
    end
end
-- CAMERA FADE: your own overlay fades exactly like your character. The camera (zooming in, first person) and
-- first-person games set LocalTransparencyModifier on the character's parts; each overlay part takes the value of
-- the real part it stands for (the body part of the same name, the matching limb on the other rig, and for an
-- accessory the body part it is worn on). A game that keeps your body visible in first person now shows the copied
-- body there, not your own; when the camera is inside the head, everything on the head stays hidden.
function Overlay.fadeLinks(entry, found)
    local model, character = entry.Model, entry.Character
    local own = entry.Target == character and found or Overlay.bodyParts(entry, character)
    local function from(list) return list and Overlay.pick(entry, list) or nil end
    local function source(name)
        local part = from(own[name]) or from(found[name])
        if part then return part end
        local group = Overlay.R6Groups[name]
        if group then return from(own[group[1]]) or from(found[group[1]]) end
        for r6, names in pairs(Overlay.R6Groups) do
            if table.find(names, name) then return from(own[r6]) or from(found[r6]) end
        end
        return nil
    end
    local mounts, links = {}, {}
    local function mountOf(accessory)
        if mounts[accessory] ~= nil then return mounts[accessory] end
        local name = false
        for _, joint in ipairs(accessory:GetDescendants()) do
            if joint:IsA("JointInstance") or joint:IsA("WeldConstraint") then
                for _, part in ipairs({joint.Part0, joint.Part1}) do
                    if part and Appearance.isBody(part, model) then name = part.Name end
                end
                if name then break end
            end
        end
        mounts[accessory] = name
        return name
    end
    -- A carried copy fades with the body part its item hangs from.
    local carriedFrom = {}
    for _, row in pairs(entry.Carried or {}) do carriedFrom[row.Copy] = row.Anchor end
    for _, part in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
---- YMLXO3K7GVTGMODEMRTGEMRUMNQTCNRZMQZWKMZSCE
        if part:IsA("BasePart") and carriedFrom[part] then
            local decals = {}
            for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do if child:IsA("Decal") then table.insert(decals, child) end end
            table.insert(links, {part, carriedFrom[part], carriedFrom[part].Name == "Head", nil, decals})
        elseif part:IsA("BasePart") and part.Name ~= "HumanoidRootPart" then
            local body = Appearance.isBody(part, model) and part.Name or nil
            if not body then
                local accessory = part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Accessory")
                body = accessory and mountOf(accessory) or nil
            end
            local decals = {}
            for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do if child:IsA("Decal") then table.insert(decals, child) end end
            table.insert(links, {part, body and source(body) or nil, body == "Head", nil, decals})
        end
    end
    entry.Fades = links
end
function Overlay.fade(entry, camera)
    local head = entry.RealHead or entry.Character:FindFirstChild("Head")
    local inside = false
    -- First person: the camera at (or just in front of) your head, or at the drawn avatar's head, which a puppet or a
    -- taller avatar holds elsewhere. Games with their own first-person camera put it a little in front of the face, and
    -- the drawn avatar's long hair then covered the whole screen.
    if camera then
        local eye = camera.CFrame.Position
        local mine = entry.Model:FindFirstChild("Head")
        if head and head.Parent and (eye - head.Position).Magnitude < 1.25 then inside = true end
        if mine and mine:IsA("BasePart") and (eye - mine.Position).Magnitude < 1.25 then inside = true end
        if lp.CameraMode == Enum.CameraMode.LockFirstPerson and entry.Character == lp.Character then inside = true end
    end
    -- A separate render model is not faded by the camera: inside its head the whole overlay hides, as before.
    local separate = entry.Target ~= entry.Character
    -- The game hiding your character (an invisibility cloak) hides the drawn avatar too.
    local hiddenByGame = entry.GameFade or 0
    for _, link in ipairs(entry.Fades or {}) do
        local value = 0
        local real = link[2]
        if real and real.Parent then
            local ok, ltm = pcall(function() return real.LocalTransparencyModifier end)
            if ok and type(ltm) == "number" then value = ltm end
        end
        if hiddenByGame > 0 then value = 1 - (1 - value) * (1 - hiddenByGame) end
        if inside and (link[3] or separate) then value = 1 end
        if link[4] ~= value then
            link[4] = value
            pcall(function() link[1].LocalTransparencyModifier = value end)
            for _, decal in ipairs(link[5]) do pcall(function() decal.LocalTransparencyModifier = value end) end
        end
    end
end
-- CARRIED ITEMS: what your character carries (a held tool, a gun in its holster, a knife on the back) would stay on
-- your hidden body: on a puppet it moved with that body's own animations, and on an avatar of the same rig, whose
-- proportions differ, it floated off the drawn hand or sank into the drawn body. Those parts are hidden there and
-- drawn on the overlay instead, each at the same place relative to the attachment it sits at (the hand's grip, the
-- back), found on the overlay by name, else relative to the matching body part. A part that leaves the character (a
-- tool put away or dropped) is shown again as the game had it.
-- Parts joined to the body that are not body parts or worn accessories, with the body part each one hangs from.
function Overlay.carriedParts(entry)
    local character = entry.Character
    local reached = {}
    for _, part in ipairs(character:GetChildren()) do
        if Appearance.isBody(part, character) then reached[part] = part end
    end
    local links = Rig.links(character)
    for _ = 1, #links + 1 do
        local changed = false
        for _, link in ipairs(links) do
            local a, b = link.A, link.B
            if reached[a] and not reached[b] then reached[b] = reached[a]; changed = true
            elseif reached[b] and not reached[a] then reached[a] = reached[b]; changed = true end
        end
        if not changed then break end
    end
    local carried = {}
    for part, anchor in pairs(reached) do
        if not Appearance.isBody(part, character) and not part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Accessory") and not part:GetAttribute("Lyra_VisualFor")
            and Overlay.original(entry, part) < 1 then
            carried[part] = anchor
        end
    end
    return carried
end
-- Where a carried part goes on the overlay: the nearest attachment of its body part that an overlay body part also
-- has, else the overlay part of the same name (or the matching limb of the other rig). Returns the real reference
-- and the overlay one.
function Overlay.carryRefs(model, attachments, anchor, part)
    local best, mine, bestDistance
    for _, attachment in ipairs(anchor:GetChildren()) do
        local match = attachment.ClassName == "Attachment" and attachments[attachment.Name]
        if match then
            local distance = (attachment.WorldPosition - part.Position).Magnitude
            if not best or distance < bestDistance then best, mine, bestDistance = attachment, match, distance end
        end
    end
    if best then return best, mine end
    local same = model:FindFirstChild(anchor.Name)
    if same and Appearance.isBody(same, model) then return anchor, same end
    local group = Overlay.R6Groups[anchor.Name]
    if group then
        local upper = model:FindFirstChild(group[1])
        if upper then return anchor, upper end
    end
    for r6, names in pairs(Overlay.R6Groups) do
        if table.find(names, anchor.Name) then
            local limb = model:FindFirstChild(r6)
            if limb then return anchor, limb end
        end
    end
    return nil, nil
end
-- A local, inert copy of a part's look (mesh, decals, surface): no scripts, joints, sounds or effects.
function Overlay.carryCopy(part)
    local ok, copy = pcall(function()
        local archivable = part.Archivable
        part.Archivable = true
        local made = part:Clone()
        part.Archivable = archivable
        return made
    end)
    if not ok or not copy then return nil end
    for _, child in ipairs(copy:GetDescendants()) do
        if not (child:IsA("DataModelMesh") or child:IsA("Decal") or child:IsA("SurfaceAppearance")) then pcall(function() child:Destroy() end) end
    end
    pcall(function()
        copy.Name = "LyraCarried"; copy.Anchored = true; copy.CanCollide = false; copy.CanTouch = false; copy.CanQuery = false; copy.Massless = true
    end)
    return copy
end
function Overlay.carry(entry)
    local old = entry.Carried or {}
    entry.Carried = nil
    if not entry.Local or (entry.Mode ~= "puppet" and entry.Mode ~= "joints") then
        for real, row in pairs(old) do
            pcall(function() row.Copy:Destroy() end)
            Overlay.unhidePart(entry, real)
            for _, decal in ipairs(row.Decals) do Overlay.unhidePart(entry, decal) end
        end
        return
    end
    local model = entry.Model
    local folder = entry.CarryFolder
    if not (folder and folder.Parent == model) then
        folder = Instance.new("Model"); folder.Name = "LyraCarried"; folder.Parent = model; entry.CarryFolder = folder
    end
    local attachments = {}
    for _, part in ipairs(model:GetChildren()) do
        if Appearance.isBody(part, model) then
            for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
                if child.ClassName == "Attachment" and not attachments[child.Name] then attachments[child.Name] = child end
            end
        end
    end
    local carried = {}
    for real, anchor in pairs(Overlay.carriedParts(entry)) do
        local row = old[real]
        if row and row.Anchor == anchor and row.Copy.Parent == folder then
            old[real] = nil
        else
            row = nil
            local realRef, mineRef = Overlay.carryRefs(model, attachments, anchor, real)
            local copy = mineRef and Overlay.carryCopy(real)
            if copy then
                copy.Parent = folder
                local decals = {}
                for _, child in ipairs(real:GetChildren()) do if child:IsA("Decal") then table.insert(decals, child) end end
                row = {Copy = copy, RealRef = realRef, MineRef = mineRef, Anchor = anchor, Decals = decals,
                    RealAttachment = realRef:IsA("Attachment"), MineAttachment = mineRef:IsA("Attachment")}
            end
        end
        if row then
            carried[real] = row
            Overlay.hidePart(entry, real, "Transparency")
            for _, decal in ipairs(row.Decals) do Overlay.hidePart(entry, decal, "Transparency") end
        end
    end
    for real, row in pairs(old) do
        pcall(function() row.Copy:Destroy() end)
        Overlay.unhidePart(entry, real)
        for _, decal in ipairs(row.Decals) do Overlay.unhidePart(entry, decal) end
    end
    entry.Carried = carried
end
-- This frame's place of every carried copy (added to the overlay's BulkMoveTo). Returns whether one went away.
function Overlay.placeCarried(entry, parts, frames)
    local stale = false
    for real, row in pairs(entry.Carried or {}) do
        if real.Parent and real:IsDescendantOf(entry.Character) and row.MineRef.Parent and row.RealRef.Parent then
            local realFrame = row.RealAttachment and row.RealRef.WorldCFrame or row.RealRef.CFrame
            local mineFrame = row.MineAttachment and row.MineRef.WorldCFrame or row.MineRef.CFrame
            parts[#parts + 1] = row.Copy; frames[#frames + 1] = mineFrame * realFrame:ToObjectSpace(real.CFrame)
            -- The game can show or hide pieces of a tool: the copy does the same.
            local shown = Overlay.original(entry, real)
            if row.Shown ~= shown then row.Shown = shown; pcall(function() row.Copy.Transparency = shown end) end
        else
            stale = true
            if row.Shown ~= 1 then row.Shown = 1; pcall(function() row.Copy.Transparency = 1 end) end
        end
    end
    return stale
end
-- The transparency a part had before the overlay hid it.
function Overlay.original(entry, item)
    if entry.HiddenProp[item] == "Transparency" then return entry.Hidden[item] end
    return item.Transparency
end
-- Body parts are normally direct children of the model. Some games nest the visible body, so for a body part with
-- no visible direct child, body-named parts deeper in the model (outside tools) are used. A visible direct child
-- keeps carried models with "Head"/"Torso" parts untouched.
function Overlay.bodyParts(entry, model)
    local direct, nested = {}, {}
    local separate = entry.Local and model ~= entry.Character
    for _, item in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
        if item:IsA("BasePart") and item.Name ~= "HumanoidRootPart" and S.BD[item.Name] ~= nil and not item:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Tool")
            and not (separate and Overlay.far(entry, item)) then
            local group = item.Parent == model and direct or nested
            local list = group[item.Name]
            if not list then list = {}; group[item.Name] = list end
            table.insert(list, item)
        end
    end
    local found = {}
    for name, list in pairs(direct) do
        local visible = false
        for _, item in ipairs(list) do if Overlay.original(entry, item) < 1 then visible = true; break end end
        found[name] = visible and list or nil
    end
    for name, list in pairs(nested) do
        if not found[name] then
            local merged = table.clone(direct[name] or {})
            for _, item in ipairs(list) do table.insert(merged, item) end
            found[name] = merged
        end
    end
    return found
end
-- Of several parts with the same name, the visible one is followed (a direct child wins a tie).
function Overlay.pick(entry, list)
    local best, bestScore
    for _, item in ipairs(list or {}) do
        local score = Overlay.original(entry, item) + (item.Parent == entry.Target and 0 or 0.001)
        if not best or score < bestScore then best, bestScore = item, score end
    end
    return best
end
-- Part0, Part1, C0 and C1 of a Motor6D or of an AnimationConstraint (the newer avatar joints).
function Overlay.jointInfo(joint)
    if joint:IsA("Motor6D") then return joint.Part0, joint.Part1, joint.C0, joint.C1 end
    local a0, a1 = joint.Attachment0, joint.Attachment1
    if a0 and a1 then return a0.Parent, a1.Parent, a0.CFrame, a1.CFrame end
end
-- Each overlay body joint is paired with the real parts of the same names (games rename or rebuild joints, and
-- newer avatars use AnimationConstraints instead of Motor6Ds). The real joint, when there is one, only lends its
-- animation offset.
function Overlay.pairJoints(entry, model, target, found, realRoot)
    local realJoints = {}
    for _, item in ipairs(target:GetDescendants()) do
        if (item:IsA("Motor6D") or item:IsA("AnimationConstraint")) and not item:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Tool") then
            local ok, a, b = pcall(Overlay.jointInfo, item)
            if ok and a and b then
                local key = a.Name .. "|" .. b.Name
                if realJoints[key] == nil then realJoints[key] = item end
            end
        end
    end
    local function realPart(name)
        if name == "HumanoidRootPart" then return realRoot end
        return Overlay.pick(entry, found[name])
    end
    local rows, total = {}, 0
    for _, item in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
        if item:IsA("Motor6D") or item:IsA("AnimationConstraint") then
            local ok, p0, p1, c0, c1 = pcall(Overlay.jointInfo, item)
            if ok and p0 and p1 and c0 and c1 and S.BD[p1.Name] ~= nil and p1.Parent == model then
                total = total + 1
                local a, b = realPart(p0.Name), realPart(p1.Name)
                if a and b then
                    local toOwn = (c0 - c0.Position):Inverse()
                    local realJoint = realJoints[p0.Name .. "|" .. p1.Name]
                    local shift
                    if realJoint then
                        local okReal, _, _, realC0 = pcall(Overlay.jointInfo, realJoint)
                        if okReal and realC0 then shift = toOwn * (realC0 - realC0.Position) end
                    end
                    table.insert(rows, {item, realJoint, a, b, toOwn, c1 - c1.Position, shift})
                end
            end
        end
    end
    return rows, total
end
function Overlay.link(entry)
    local character, model = entry.Character, entry.Model
    -- Your own overlay also hides (and may follow) any other copy of your body (see the world scan).
    if entry.Local then entry.Extra = Overlay.bodies(character, true, entry) end
    local target = Overlay.target(character, entry.Extra)
    entry.Target = target
    if entry.Local then pcall(Overlay.releaseCopies, entry) end
    local root, realRoot = model:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart"), Overlay.rootOf(character)
    entry.Root, entry.RealRoot = root, realRoot
    local found = Overlay.bodyParts(entry, target)
    entry.FoundParts = found
    entry.Found = next(found) ~= nil or realRoot ~= nil
    entry.RealHead = Overlay.pick(entry, found.Head)
    Overlay.linkMode(entry, target, found, root, realRoot)
    -- What the character carries goes on a puppet (see CARRIED ITEMS); then the camera fade links.
    if entry.Local then Overlay.carry(entry); Overlay.fadeLinks(entry, found) end
end
function Overlay.linkMode(entry, target, found, root, realRoot)
    local character, model = entry.Character, entry.Model
    if Overlay.wantsPuppet(entry, target) and root and realRoot then
        Overlay.setMode(entry, "puppet")
        local own = model:GetAttribute("LyraStandHeight") or Overlay.standHeight(model)
        local real = Overlay.standHeight(target) or Overlay.standHeight(character)
        entry.Lift = CFrame.new(0, (own and real) and (own - real) or 0, 0)
        entry.Joints, entry.Links, entry.Limbs = {}, {}, nil
        return
    end
    local rows, total = Overlay.pairJoints(entry, model, target, found, realRoot)
    -- A separate render model (Evade) moves its parts itself, sliding and crouching included: parts mode follows it
    -- exactly. Joints mode is for characters whose own body is the visible one, unless it stood frozen on this
    -- character before (see FROZEN AVATAR).
    if not entry.ForceParts and target == character and root and realRoot and realRoot.Name == "HumanoidRootPart" and total >= 5 and #rows >= total * 0.8 then
        if entry.Local and entry.Mode ~= "joints" then
            App.devNote(string.format("Visual-only follows the joints: %d of %d joints paired.", #rows, total))
        end
        Overlay.setMode(entry, "joints")
        -- The overlay's lowest point lands where the character stands: never above it, never pushed below it.
        local own, real = model:GetAttribute("LyraStandHeight") or Overlay.standHeight(model), Overlay.standHeight(character)
        entry.Lift = CFrame.new(0, (own and real) and (own - real) or 0, 0)
        -- Each overlay joint gets the rotation the game's limb really has relative to its parent part, expressed in
        -- the overlay joint's own axes. Games build joints with different C0/C1 axes, so copying Transform as is
        -- would twist the limbs.
        entry.Joints, entry.Links = rows, {}
        return
    end
    if entry.Local and entry.Mode ~= "parts" then
        App.devNote(string.format("Visual-only follows the parts (%s; %d of %d joints paired).",
            entry.ForceParts and "it stood frozen on the joints" or target ~= character and "a separate body" or "too few joints", #rows, total))
    end
    Overlay.setMode(entry, "parts")
    -- SOLVED POSE: an avatar that stood frozen on the joints used to be put part by part on your own body parts, so an
    -- avatar of other proportions came apart (gaps at the shoulders and hips, limbs inside the torso). Its pose is now
    -- worked out here instead: each of its parts is placed from its parent through its own joint, with the rotation
    -- your limb really has, so it keeps its own shape and moves as the joints mode would.
    local solved = {}
    entry.Solve = nil
    if entry.ForceParts and target == character and root and realRoot and total >= 5 and #rows >= total * 0.8 then
        local pending, order, placed = {}, {}, {[root] = true}
        for _, row in ipairs(rows) do
            local ok, p0, p1, c0, c1 = pcall(Overlay.jointInfo, row[1])
            if ok and p0 and p1 and c0 and c1 then table.insert(pending, {p0, p1, c0, c1:Inverse(), row[3], row[4], row[5], row[6], row[7], row[2]}) end
        end
        local moved = true
        while moved do
            moved = false
            for index = #pending, 1, -1 do
                local row = pending[index]
                if placed[row[1]] and not placed[row[2]] then
                    placed[row[2]] = true; table.insert(order, row); table.remove(pending, index); moved = true
                end
            end
        end
        if #order >= total * 0.8 then
            entry.Solve = order
            -- The avatar's lowest point lands where the character stands, as on the joints.
            local own, real = model:GetAttribute("LyraStandHeight") or Overlay.standHeight(model), Overlay.standHeight(character)
            entry.Lift = CFrame.new(0, (own and real) and (own - real) or 0, 0)
            for _, row in ipairs(order) do solved[row[2]] = true end
        end
    end
    -- Parts the target does not have follow the character's root with their rest-pose offset.
    local links = {}
    for _, part in ipairs(model:GetChildren()) do
        if part:IsA("BasePart") and part.Anchored and not solved[part] then
            local real = part.Name == "HumanoidRootPart" and realRoot or Overlay.pick(entry, found[part.Name])
            local mapped, offset
            if not real then mapped, offset = Overlay.crossRig(entry, model, part, found) end
            if real then table.insert(links, {part, real})
            elseif mapped then table.insert(links, {part, mapped, offset})
            elseif root and realRoot then table.insert(links, {part, realRoot, root.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(part.CFrame)})
            else part.Transparency = 1 end
        end
    end
    entry.Joints, entry.Links = {}, links
end
-- An R6 limb is one part; the matching R15 limb is three. Lists start with the upper part.
Overlay.R6Groups = {Torso = {"UpperTorso", "LowerTorso"}, ["Left Arm"] = {"LeftUpperArm", "LeftLowerArm", "LeftHand"},
    ["Right Arm"] = {"RightUpperArm", "RightLowerArm", "RightHand"}, ["Left Leg"] = {"LeftUpperLeg", "LeftLowerLeg", "LeftFoot"},
    ["Right Leg"] = {"RightUpperLeg", "RightLowerLeg", "RightFoot"}}
-- An overlay part with no real part of the same name (an R6 avatar on an R15 body or the other way round) follows
-- the matching limb, with the tops of both limbs lined up. Returns the real part and the offset from it.
function Overlay.crossRig(entry, model, part, found)
    local group = Overlay.R6Groups[part.Name]
    if group then
        local real = Overlay.pick(entry, found[group[1]])
        if real then return real, CFrame.new(0, real.Size.Y / 2 - part.Size.Y / 2, 0) end
        return nil
    end
    local rest = part:GetAttribute("LyraRest")
    if typeof(rest) ~= "CFrame" then return nil end
    for r6, names in pairs(Overlay.R6Groups) do
        if table.find(names, part.Name) then
            local real = Overlay.pick(entry, found[r6])
            local upper = model:FindFirstChild(names[1])
            local upperRest = upper and upper:GetAttribute("LyraRest")
            if not real or typeof(upperRest) ~= "CFrame" then return nil end
            local top = upperRest.Position + Vector3.new(0, upper.Size.Y / 2, 0)
            return real, CFrame.new(0, real.Size.Y / 2, 0) * CFrame.new(-top) * rest
        end
    end
end
-- FAR BODIES: with an avatar drawn over your character, other copies of your body are hidden and may be followed, but
-- only where you stand. A part of such a model that is more than 12 studs from your character is not your body here: a
-- rhythm game keeps the body it shows on its stage inside a model that stays at your feet (Project Afternight's
-- "Rig.PlayerRig", hundreds of studs away). It was hidden with the rest, so the stage showed nobody, and the stand-ins
-- that then dressed it had every part written back to invisible by the overlay. Far parts are now left alone, shown
-- again if they were hidden, and never followed.
function Overlay.far(entry, part)
    local root = entry.RealRoot
    if not (root and root.Parent) then root = Overlay.rootOf(entry.Character) end
    return root ~= nil and (part.Position - root.Position).Magnitude > 12
end
-- A model the stand-ins take over stops being the overlay's: everything hidden in it shows again as the game has it.
function Overlay.forget(model)
    local character = lp.Character
    local entry = character and Overlay.Active[character]
    if not entry or not entry.Local or model == character then return end
    if entry.Kept then entry.Kept[model] = nil end
    local items = {}
    for item in pairs(entry.Hidden) do if item:IsDescendantOf(model) then table.insert(items, item) end end
    for _, item in ipairs(items) do Overlay.unhidePart(entry, item) end
    for item, guard in pairs(entry.HideGuards or {}) do
        if item:IsDescendantOf(model) then guard:Disconnect(); entry.HideGuards[item] = nil end
    end
end
-- STAGE COPIES: rhythm games (and lobbies, cutscenes) copy your character where you stand and then put the copy
-- somewhere else: on the stage, while your own character waits out of sight. With an avatar drawn over your character
-- (visual-only, or an R15 avatar in an R6 game) such a copy was hidden as another copy of your body and stayed hidden
-- wherever the game took it, and a copy made of your hidden body was invisible from the start, so the stage showed
-- nobody. A copy that is no longer where you stand is now shown again as the game made it and handed to the stand-ins
-- (see STAND-INS), which put the avatar you wear on it. It has to be well away (8 studs) on two looks in a row, about
-- a second apart, so a body that only lags behind you for a moment stays the overlay's.
function Overlay.releaseCopies(entry)
    entry.Kept = entry.Kept or setmetatable({}, {__mode = "k"})
    for _, model in ipairs(entry.Extra or {}) do entry.Kept[model] = 0 end
    local root = Overlay.rootOf(entry.Character)
    if not root then return end
    local gone = {}
    for model, away in pairs(entry.Kept) do
        if not model.Parent then entry.Kept[model] = nil
        elseif model ~= entry.Target and not table.find(entry.Extra or {}, model) then
            local other = Overlay.rootOf(model)
            if other and (other.Position - root.Position).Magnitude > 8 then
                if away >= 1 then table.insert(gone, model) else entry.Kept[model] = away + 1 end
            else entry.Kept[model] = 0 end
        end
    end
    for _, model in ipairs(gone) do
        entry.Kept[model] = nil
        local items = {}
        for item in pairs(entry.Hidden) do if item:IsDescendantOf(model) then table.insert(items, item) end end
        for _, item in ipairs(items) do Overlay.unhidePart(entry, item) end
        if App.tracing() then App.trace("Stage copy left your place and is shown again: " .. App.traceName(model)) end
        Mirror.Tries[model] = nil
        Mirror.queue(model, 0.2)
    end
end
-- A copy the game made of your character while the overlay kept it hidden carries the hidden values (the mask on body
-- parts, 1 on worn items). It gets the values the game's own character had. Returns whether the model is such a copy.
function Overlay.unmaskCopy(model)
    local character = lp.Character
    local entry = character and Overlay.Active[character]
    if not entry or not entry.Local or model == character then return false end
    local masked = false
    for _, part in ipairs(model:GetChildren()) do
        if part:IsA("BasePart") and S.BD[part.Name] and part:GetAttribute("Lyra_BeforeOverlay") == nil and isMask(part.Transparency) then masked = true; break end
    end
    if not masked then return false end
    for _, item in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
        if (item:IsA("BasePart") or item:IsA("Decal")) and item.Transparency > 0.99 and not entry.Hidden[item] then
            -- The same part of your own character, by its path of names.
            local names, cursor = {}, item
            while cursor and cursor ~= model do table.insert(names, 1, cursor.Name); cursor = cursor.Parent end
            local twin = character
            for _, name in ipairs(names) do twin = twin and twin:FindFirstChild(name) end
            local value = twin and twin ~= character and entry.HiddenProp[twin] == "Transparency" and entry.Hidden[twin] or nil
            if type(value) == "number" and value < 0.99 then pcall(function() item.Transparency = value end)
            elseif isMask(item.Transparency) then pcall(function() item.Transparency = 0 end) end
        end
    end
    return true
end
-- DRAWN OVER SOMEONE ELSE: an avatar drawn over a script user's character or over a stand-in is not faded by the
-- camera, but it follows the game: when the game hides or fades that whole body (a stage copy waiting for its song, an
-- invisibility power), the drawn avatar hides or fades as much. The least hidden body part counts, so a body with one
-- part the game always hides still shows. A separate body the overlay hides itself is read as the game has it.
function Overlay.fadeRemote(entry)
    local target = entry.Target and entry.Target.Parent and entry.Target or entry.Character
    local least, count = 1, 0
    for _, part in ipairs(target:GetChildren()) do
        if part:IsA("BasePart") and part.Name ~= "HumanoidRootPart" and S.BD[part.Name] ~= nil then
            least = math.min(least, Overlay.original(entry, part)); count = count + 1
        end
    end
    -- A body the game draws on parts nested deeper in the model (see Overlay.bodyParts).
    for _, list in pairs(entry.FoundParts or {}) do
        for _, part in ipairs(list) do
            if part.Parent and part.Parent ~= target then least = math.min(least, Overlay.original(entry, part)); count = count + 1 end
        end
    end
    local value = count > 0 and math.clamp(least, 0, 1) or 0
    if value < 0.005 then value = 0 end
    if entry.RemoteFade == value and entry.RemoteFadeFor == entry.Model then return end
    -- Nothing to write on an overlay that was never faded.
    local fresh = entry.RemoteFadeFor ~= entry.Model
    entry.RemoteFade, entry.RemoteFadeFor = value, entry.Model
    if fresh and value == 0 then return end
    for _, item in ipairs(entry.Model:GetDescendants()) do
        if item:IsA("BasePart") or item:IsA("Decal") then pcall(function() item.LocalTransparencyModifier = value end) end
    end
end
-- The visible body and accessories are hidden while the overlay is shown: your own character with Transparency
-- (the camera rewrites LocalTransparencyModifier on it), other players' characters with LocalTransparencyModifier,
-- and a separate render model (local to this client) with Transparency.
-- Hides one part or decal for an overlay. A game that shows it again (on a cosmetic change, or every frame) is undone
-- at once: only the copier writes 1, so any other value is the game's, kept for when the overlay comes off.
-- Your own body parts are hidden with the mask (Cloak.Mask) instead of 1, so the game making your character invisible (setting 1, an
-- invisibility cloak) still shows as a change, and the drawn avatar disappears with it (see Overlay.gameFade).
function Overlay.hidePart(entry, item, property)
    entry.HideGuards = entry.HideGuards or {}
    entry.Normal = entry.Normal or {}
    local character = entry.Character
    local ok, current = pcall(function() return item[property] end)
    if not ok then return end
    local hidden = (property == "Transparency" and entry.Local and item.Parent == character and Appearance.isBody(item, character)) and Cloak.Mask or 1
    if not entry.HideGuards[item] then
        local guarded, connection = pcall(function()
            return item:GetPropertyChangedSignal(property):Connect(function()
                if Overlay.Active[character] ~= entry then return end
                local value = item[property]
                -- Compared with a tolerance: the property keeps a 32-bit float (see Cloak.Mask).
                if math.abs(value - hidden) > 1e-4 then
                    entry.Hidden[item] = value; entry.HiddenProp[item] = property; item[property] = hidden
                    if hidden ~= 1 then Overlay.gameFade(entry) end
                end
            end)
        end)
        if guarded then entry.HideGuards[item] = connection end
    end
    if math.abs(current - hidden) < 1e-4 then return end
    if entry.Hidden[item] == nil then
        entry.Hidden[item] = current; entry.HiddenProp[item] = property
        -- What the game shows when the overlay first hides it: its usual value.
        if entry.Normal[item] == nil then entry.Normal[item] = current end
    end
    pcall(function() item[property] = hidden end)
end
-- How much the game hides your own character (0 to 1): the least hidden of the body parts it usually shows. The drawn
-- avatar fades as much (see Overlay.fade).
function Overlay.gameFade(entry)
    local least, count = 1, 0
    for item, normal in pairs(entry.Normal or {}) do
        local value = entry.Hidden[item]
        if type(normal) == "number" and normal < 0.5 and type(value) == "number" and entry.HiddenProp[item] == "Transparency"
            and Appearance.isBody(item, entry.Character) then
            least = math.min(least, math.clamp((value - normal) / (1 - normal), 0, 1)); count = count + 1
        end
    end
    entry.GameFade = count > 0 and least or 0
end
-- Shows a hidden part again as the game had it (an item that left your character, such as a dropped tool).
function Overlay.unhidePart(entry, item)
    local guard = entry.HideGuards and entry.HideGuards[item]
    if guard then guard:Disconnect(); entry.HideGuards[item] = nil end
    local old, property = entry.Hidden[item], entry.HiddenProp[item]
    entry.Hidden[item] = nil; entry.HiddenProp[item] = nil
    if old ~= nil and property then pcall(function() item[property] = old end) end
end
function Overlay.hide(entry)
-- YMLXO3K7GVTGMODEMRTGEMRUMNQTCNRZMQZWKMZSCE
    local character = entry.Character
    local function hide(item, property) Overlay.hidePart(entry, item, property) end
    local function sweep(model)
        local property = (model ~= character or entry.Local) and "Transparency" or "LocalTransparencyModifier"
        -- Another model's parts far from you are not your body here (see FAR BODIES).
        local separate = entry.Local and model ~= character
        local function away(part) return separate and part:IsA("BasePart") and Overlay.far(entry, part) end
        for _, list in pairs(Overlay.bodyParts(entry, model)) do
            for _, part in ipairs(list) do
                hide(part, property)
                for _, decal in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do if decal:IsA("Decal") then hide(decal, property) end end
            end
        end
        for _, item in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
            if item:IsA("Accessory") and not item:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Tool") then
                local handle = item:FindFirstChild("Handle")
                if not (handle and away(handle)) then
                    for _, child in ipairs(item:GetDescendants()) do if child:IsA("BasePart") or child:IsA("Decal") then hide(child, property) end end
                end
            end
        end
        if separate then
            local gone = {}
            for item in pairs(entry.Hidden) do
                local part = item:IsA("Decal") and item.Parent or item
                if item:IsDescendantOf(model) and part and away(part) then table.insert(gone, item) end
            end
            for _, item in ipairs(gone) do Overlay.unhidePart(entry, item) end
        end
    end
    sweep(character)
    local swept = {[character] = true}
    if entry.Target and entry.Target ~= character and entry.Target.Parent then sweep(entry.Target); swept[entry.Target] = true end
    -- Other copies of your body standing where you are (a game can draw it on a separate model, see Overlay.bodies).
    for _, model in ipairs(entry.Extra or {}) do
        if not swept[model] and model.Parent then sweep(model); swept[model] = true end
    end
end
-- Keeps every overlay part out of physics, raycasts and touches, even if something switches them back on.
function Overlay.inert(entry)
    for _, item in ipairs(entry.Model:GetDescendants()) do
        if item:IsA("BasePart") and (item.CanCollide or item.CanQuery or item.CanTouch) then
            item.CanCollide = false; item.CanQuery = false; item.CanTouch = false
        end
    end
end
-- Every overlay part stays out of physics at once and for good: a part that something switches back to colliding
-- (a Humanoid does this to R6 torsos and heads) is switched off again in the same frame, so the overlay never pushes
-- the character it is drawn on.
function Overlay.guard(entry)
    for _, connection in ipairs(entry.Guards or {}) do connection:Disconnect() end
    entry.Guards = {}
    for _, part in ipairs(entry.Model:GetDescendants()) do
        if part:IsA("BasePart") then
            part.CanCollide = false; part.CanTouch = false; part.CanQuery = false
            table.insert(entry.Guards, part:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CanCollide"):Connect(function()
                if part.CanCollide then part.CanCollide = false end
            end))
        end
    end
end
-- Where the overlay's parts go this frame (added to parts/frames for one BulkMoveTo). Returns whether a followed part
-- is gone (the overlay then relinks).
function Overlay.place(entry, parts, frames)
    local stale = false
    if entry.Mode == "joints" or entry.Mode == "puppet" then
        local realRoot = entry.RealRoot
        if realRoot and realRoot.Parent then parts[#parts + 1] = entry.Root; frames[#frames + 1] = realRoot.CFrame * entry.Lift
        else stale = true end
        -- A puppet's joints are moved by its own animations.
        for _, row in ipairs(entry.Joints) do
            local a, b = row[3], row[4]
            if a.Parent and b.Parent then
                local relative = a.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(b.CFrame)
                local turn = row[5] * (relative - relative.Position) * row[6]
                local real = row[2]
                if row[7] and real and real.Parent then turn = CFrame.new(row[7] * real.Transform.Position) * turn end
                row[1].Transform = turn
            else stale = true end
        end
    else
        for _, link in ipairs(entry.Links) do
            if link[2].Parent then parts[#parts + 1] = link[1]; frames[#frames + 1] = link[3] and link[2].CFrame * link[3] or link[2].CFrame
            else stale = true end
        end
        -- See SOLVED POSE: parents first, each part from its parent's place this frame.
        if entry.Solve then
            local realRoot = entry.RealRoot
            if realRoot and realRoot.Parent and entry.Root then
                local at = {[entry.Root] = realRoot.CFrame * (entry.Lift or CFrame.new())}
                for _, row in ipairs(entry.Solve) do
                    local parent, a, b = at[row[1]], row[5], row[6]
                    if parent and a.Parent and b.Parent then
                        local relative = a.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(b.CFrame)
                        local turn = row[7] * (relative - relative.Position) * row[8]
                        local real = row[10]
                        if row[9] and real and real.Parent then turn = CFrame.new(row[9] * real.Transform.Position) * turn end
                        local frame = parent * row[3] * turn * row[4]
                        at[row[2]] = frame
                        parts[#parts + 1] = row[2]; frames[#frames + 1] = frame
                    else stale = true end
                end
            else stale = true end
        end
    end
    if entry.Carried and Overlay.placeCarried(entry, parts, frames) then stale = true end
    return stale
end
function Overlay.attach(character, model, isLocal, key, extra)
    Overlay.clear(character)
    local entry = {Character = character, Model = model, Links = {}, Joints = {}, Hidden = {}, HiddenProp = {}, Local = isLocal, Key = key, Started = os.clock(), Revives = {}}
    for field, value in pairs(extra or {}) do entry[field] = value end
    -- A tool taken out or put away is moved onto the overlay (or shown again) on the next frame.
    if isLocal then
        entry.Watch = {}
        for _, event in ipairs({character.ChildAdded, character.ChildRemoved}) do
            table.insert(entry.Watch, event:Connect(function(child) if child:IsA("Tool") then entry.Relink = true end end))
        end
    end
    local copied, spare = pcall(function() return model:Clone() end)
    entry.Spare = copied and spare or nil
    Overlay.Active[character] = entry
    Overlay.guard(entry)
    Overlay.link(entry)
    Overlay.hide(entry)
    -- Placed at once, so it never shows (or sits) at the world origin for a frame.
    pcall(function()
        local parts, frames = {}, {}
        Overlay.place(entry, parts, frames)
        if #parts > 0 then workspace:BulkMoveTo(parts, frames, Enum.BulkMoveMode.FireCFrameChanged) end
    end)
    Overlay.start()
    return entry
end
-- The game removed the overlay (cleared the camera, for example): put it back, or rebuild it from the spare copy.
-- At most 20 times a minute, so a game that deletes it on every frame does not make it rebuild forever.
function Overlay.revive(entry)
    local now = os.clock()
    for i = #entry.Revives, 1, -1 do if now - entry.Revives[i] > 60 then table.remove(entry.Revives, i) end end
    if #entry.Revives >= 20 then return false end
    table.insert(entry.Revives, now)
    local moved = pcall(function() entry.Model.Parent = Overlay.folder() end)
    if not moved or not entry.Model:IsDescendantOf(workspace) then
        if not entry.Spare then return false end
        local copied, model = pcall(function() return entry.Spare:Clone() end)
        if not copied or not model then return false end
        pcall(function() entry.Model:Destroy() end)
        model.Parent = Overlay.folder(); entry.Model = model; entry.Mode = nil
        Overlay.guard(entry)
    end
    Overlay.link(entry)
    return true
end
function Overlay.clear(character)
    local entry = character and Overlay.Active[character]
    if not entry then return end
    Overlay.Active[character] = nil
    if entry.Puppet then pcall(Overlay.puppetStop, entry) end
    for _, connection in ipairs(entry.Watch or {}) do connection:Disconnect() end
    for _, connection in ipairs(entry.Guards or {}) do connection:Disconnect() end
    for _, connection in pairs(entry.HideGuards or {}) do connection:Disconnect() end
    for item, old in pairs(entry.Hidden) do
        local property = entry.HiddenProp[item]
        pcall(function() if item.Parent then item[property] = old end end)
    end
    pcall(function() entry.Model:Destroy() end)
    if entry.Spare then pcall(function() entry.Spare:Destroy() end) end
end
function Overlay.clearAll()
    for character in pairs(Overlay.Active) do Overlay.clear(character) end
    if Overlay.Connection then Overlay.Connection:Disconnect(); Overlay.Connection = nil end
    if Overlay.Folder then pcall(function() Overlay.Folder:Destroy() end); Overlay.Folder = nil end
end
function Overlay.start()
    if Overlay.Connection then return end
    local frame = 0
    Overlay.Connection = RS.RenderStepped:Connect(function()
        frame = frame + 1
        -- The shared world scan moves on a little every frame.
        pcall(Overlay.scanStep, 800)
        local parts, frames = {}, {}
        local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
        for character, entry in pairs(Overlay.Active) do
            if not character.Parent then
                Overlay.clear(character)
            elseif not entry.Model.Parent or not entry.Model:IsDescendantOf(workspace) then
                if not Overlay.revive(entry) then
                    Overlay.clear(character)
                    if entry.Local then App.report("The game keeps removing the avatar drawn over your character, so it was turned off.", "warning") end
                end
            else
                if entry.Relink then entry.Relink = nil; pcall(Overlay.link, entry) end
                local stale = Overlay.place(entry, parts, frames)
                if entry.Target ~= character and not (entry.Target and entry.Target.Parent) then stale = true end
                -- Twice a second (your own overlay: six times): relink when parts were rebuilt (or while a render model
                -- has not appeared yet), hide what loaded late or was reset, and keep the overlay out of physics.
                if frame % (entry.Local and 10 or 30) == 0 then
                    Overlay.folder()
                    -- A render model or another copy of your body can appear later (a game may build it once you
                    -- play or change a cosmetic): your own overlay looks again every second.
                    if stale or not entry.Found or (entry.Local and frame % 60 == 0) then Overlay.link(entry) end
                    if entry.Local then pcall(Overlay.watchStiff, entry); pcall(Overlay.checkFollow, entry) end
                    Overlay.hide(entry); Overlay.inert(entry)
                    if entry.Local and not entry.Found and not entry.Warned and os.clock() - entry.Started > 6 then
                        entry.Warned = true
                        App.report("Your character could not be found in this game yet, so the avatar is not drawn. It appears once your character does.", "warning")
                    end
                end
                if entry.Mode == "puppet" then pcall(Overlay.puppetStep, entry); pcall(Overlay.puppetLimbs, entry) end
                if entry.Mood and frame % 15 == 0 then pcall(Overlay.playMood, entry) end
                -- Your own overlay fades with your character (zooming in, first person; see CAMERA FADE); one drawn
                -- over someone else follows the game hiding that body (see DRAWN OVER SOMEONE ELSE).
                if entry.Local then pcall(Overlay.fade, entry, camera)
                elseif frame % 2 == 0 then pcall(Overlay.fadeRemote, entry) end
            end
        end
        if #parts > 0 then pcall(function() workspace:BulkMoveTo(parts, frames, Enum.BulkMoveMode.FireCFrameChanged) end) end
        if next(Overlay.Active) == nil and Overlay.Connection then Overlay.Connection:Disconnect(); Overlay.Connection = nil end
    end)
end

-- CUSTOM CHARACTERS: some games draw your character their own way, so an avatar put on the character itself cannot show
-- (or shows mixed with the game's body). Visual-only draws it over the character instead, and is suggested once per game
-- in a session, with a button that turns it on. Only on clear signs, read before the avatar goes on: a separate model
-- joined to your character's root draws your body (Evade's way), your own body parts are all hidden while another body
-- is drawn where you stand, or the character has no Roblox body parts at all. A game whose character merely looks
-- unusual, or hides your body only in first person, is never told to.
App.SuggestedVisual = {}
function App.customCharacter(char)
    if not char or not char.Parent then return nil end
    local ok, rig, linked = pcall(Overlay.renderRig, char)
    if ok and rig and linked then return "render" end
    local parts, shown = 0, 0
    for _, part in ipairs(char:GetChildren()) do
        if part:IsA("BasePart") and S.BD[part.Name] and part.Name ~= "HumanoidRootPart" then
            parts = parts + 1
            if part.Transparency < 1 then shown = shown + 1 end
        end
    end
    if parts == 0 then return char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") and "nobody" or nil end
    if shown == 0 then
        local found, others = pcall(Overlay.bodies, char, false)
        if found and type(others) == "table" and #others > 0 then return "hidden" end
    end
    return nil
end
function App.suggestVisualOnly(reason)
    if not reason or Overlay.visualOnly() or App.SuggestedVisual[game.GameId] or not App.alive() then return end
    App.SuggestedVisual[game.GameId] = true
    App.toast({Title = "Visual-only works better here", Kind = "info", Icon = "eye-off", Duration = 12,
        Text = "This game draws your character its own way, so an avatar put on the character itself may not show right. Visual-only draws it over your character instead.",
        Action = {Text = "Turn on Visual-only", Callback = function()
            if Overlay.visualOnly() or not App.alive() then return end
            Store.Settings.VisualOnly = true; App.persist()
            if UI.Toggles and UI.Toggles.VisualOnly then pcall(UI.Toggles.VisualOnly) end
            App.switchVisualOnly(true)
        end}})
end

-- CAMERA ON A FLOATING AVATAR: Roblox's camera follows the HumanoidRootPart, not the body. An animation pack that floats
-- (Floating Aura, Levitation…) lifts the body above it, so with such an avatar on, the camera stayed below the floating
-- head. While a copied avatar is on your character itself (not visual-only), a lift the animation holds (the root
-- joint raising the body more than 0.3 studs) raises the camera by as much, eased in and out, through the Humanoid's
-- CameraOffset. Short moves (a walk's bounce, a jump) and every avatar that does not float change nothing, and nothing
-- is written then. What the game puts in CameraOffset is kept; the lift comes off with the avatar.
local CameraLift = {Added = 0, Smooth = 0}
function CameraLift.rootJoint(char)
    if CameraLift.JointFor == char and CameraLift.Joint and CameraLift.Joint.Parent then return CameraLift.Joint end
    -- A rig without that joint is looked at again once a second, not every frame (a search of the whole character).
    if CameraLift.JointFor == char and not CameraLift.Joint and os.clock() < (CameraLift.RetryAt or 0) then return nil end
    CameraLift.JointFor, CameraLift.Joint, CameraLift.RetryAt = char, nil, os.clock() + 1
    local root = char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
    local torso = char:FindFirstChild("LowerTorso") or char:FindFirstChild("Torso")
    if not root or not torso then return nil end
    -- The root joint sits in the torso (R15) or the root (R6); the rest of the character only when a game moved it.
    for _, holder in ipairs({torso, root}) do
        for _, item in ipairs(holder:GetChildren()) do
            if item:IsA("Motor6D") and item.Part0 == root and item.Part1 == torso then CameraLift.Joint = item; return item end
        end
    end
    for _, item in ipairs(char:GetDescendants()) do
        if item:IsA("Motor6D") and item.Part0 == root and item.Part1 == torso then CameraLift.Joint = item; break end
    end
    return CameraLift.Joint
end
-- How far the animation holds the body above its rest place, in studs (0 when it does not).
function CameraLift.lift(char)
    local joint = CameraLift.rootJoint(char)
    if not joint then return 0 end
    local ok, value = pcall(function()
        local base = joint.Part0.CFrame * joint.C0
        return (base * joint.Transform).Position.Y - base.Position.Y
    end)
    return (ok and value > 0.3) and value or 0
end
function CameraLift.step(dt)
    local char = lp.Character
    local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if hum ~= CameraLift.Hum then CameraLift.Hum, CameraLift.Added, CameraLift.Smooth, CameraLift.LastSet = hum, 0, 0, nil end
    if not hum then return end
    local active = S.fvOn and S.TouchedChar == char and not Overlay.visualOnly() and hum.Health > 0
    local lift = active and CameraLift.lift(char) or 0
    CameraLift.Smooth = CameraLift.Smooth + (lift - CameraLift.Smooth) * math.min(1, (dt or 0) * 3)
    local want = CameraLift.Smooth > 0.05 and CameraLift.Smooth or 0
    if want == 0 and CameraLift.Added == 0 then return end
    local current = hum.CameraOffset
    -- A value the game set since (not the one written here) is the game's own, without the lift.
    local base = (CameraLift.LastSet and (current - CameraLift.LastSet).Magnitude < 1e-3) and (current - Vector3.new(0, CameraLift.Added, 0)) or current
    local target = base + Vector3.new(0, want, 0)
    if (target - current).Magnitude > 0.01 or (want == 0 and CameraLift.Added ~= 0) then
        hum.CameraOffset = target
        CameraLift.LastSet, CameraLift.Added = target, want
    else
--- YMLXO3K7GVTGMODEMRTGEMRUMNQTCNRZMQZWKMZSCE
        -- Too small a change to write: what stays applied is what is there.
        CameraLift.LastSet, CameraLift.Added = current, current.Y - base.Y
    end
end
-- Takes the lift off at once (the script closing).
function CameraLift.reset()
    local hum = CameraLift.Hum
    if hum and hum.Parent and CameraLift.Added ~= 0 and CameraLift.LastSet and (hum.CameraOffset - CameraLift.LastSet).Magnitude < 1e-3 then
        hum.CameraOffset = hum.CameraOffset - Vector3.new(0, CameraLift.Added, 0)
    end
    CameraLift.Added, CameraLift.Smooth, CameraLift.LastSet = 0, 0, nil
end
RegisterConnection(RS.RenderStepped:Connect(function(dt) if App.alive() then pcall(CameraLift.step, dt) end end))

-- STAND-INS: games build more copies of your avatar than your character: a lobby or menu preview, intro cutscenes, a
-- first-person body. They are usually made from your Roblox profile on the server, so they kept showing your own
-- avatar while you wore another one. Any model with a Humanoid that is not a player's character and shows you is
-- dressed in the avatar you wear, on your screen only; its joints and animations stay the game's, so a cutscene plays
-- as made. It gets its own look back with yours. A model shows you when it is named after you, carries your avatar's
-- description, or wears at least three pieces of your own avatar (two of them accessories).
-- Settings > Advanced > "Show my avatar on the game's copies of me" turns this off, your in-game picture included.
Mirror.Known = setmetatable({}, {__mode = "k"})
Mirror.Dressed = setmetatable({}, {__mode = "k"})
Mirror.Tries = setmetatable({}, {__mode = "k"})
Mirror.Queue, Mirror.Queued = {}, setmetatable({}, {__mode = "k"})
Mirror.Sources, Mirror.OwnKeys = {}, {}
Mirror.Unmasked = setmetatable({}, {__mode = "k"})
function Mirror.wanted()
    return Store.Settings.StandIns ~= false and App.Current ~= nil and not App.Current.Original
end
-- An asset id from a content URL (rbxassetid://1, http://www.roblox.com/asset/?id=1), else the URL itself.
function Mirror.assetKey(url)
    local text = tostring(url or "")
    return text:match("^rbxassetid://(%d+)") or text:match("[?&]id=(%d+)") or text:match("^(%d+)$") or text
end
-- The pieces a model wears: clothing templates and accessory meshes. Pieces the copier added never count.
function Mirror.pieces(model)
    local set, count = {}, 0
    local function add(key, kind)
        if key ~= "" and not set[key] then set[key] = kind; count = count + 1 end
    end
    for _, item in ipairs(model:GetChildren()) do
        if not item:GetAttribute("Copier_CopiedItem") then
            if item:IsA("Shirt") and item.ShirtTemplate ~= "" then add("shirt:" .. Mirror.assetKey(item.ShirtTemplate), "cloth")
            elseif item:IsA("Pants") and item.PantsTemplate ~= "" then add("pants:" .. Mirror.assetKey(item.PantsTemplate), "cloth")
            elseif item:IsA("ShirtGraphic") and item.Graphic ~= "" then add("tee:" .. Mirror.assetKey(item.Graphic), "cloth")
            elseif item:IsA("Accessory") then
                local handle = item:FindFirstChild("Handle")
                local mesh
                if handle and handle:IsA("MeshPart") then mesh = handle.MeshId
                elseif handle then
                    local special = handle:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("SpecialMesh")
                    mesh = special and special.MeshId
                end
                if mesh and mesh ~= "" then add("acc:" .. Mirror.assetKey(mesh), "acc") end
            end
        end
    end
    return {Set = set, Count = count}
end
-- What a description dresses: clothing, face, body parts and accessories. An avatar that wears almost nothing says
-- nothing about whose it is, so it gives no key.
function Mirror.descKey(desc)
    local parts, worn = {}, 0
    local ok = pcall(function()
        for _, field in ipairs({"Shirt", "Pants", "GraphicTShirt", "Face", "Head", "Torso", "LeftArm", "RightArm", "LeftLeg", "RightLeg"}) do
            local value = tostring(desc[field])
            table.insert(parts, value)
            if value ~= "0" then worn = worn + 1 end
        end
        local ids = {}
        for _, row in ipairs(desc:GetAccessories(true)) do table.insert(ids, tostring(row.AssetId)) end
        table.sort(ids)
        worn = worn + #ids
        table.insert(parts, table.concat(ids, ","))
    end)
    return (ok and worn >= 3) and table.concat(parts, "|") or ""
end
-- Remembers your own look while the copier has not changed your character.
function Mirror.learn(char)
    if not char or S.TouchedChar == char then return end
    local hum = char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    local live = hum and App.liveDescription(hum)
    if live and not live:GetAttribute("Lyra_Description") then
        local key = Mirror.descKey(live)
        if key ~= "" then Mirror.OwnKeys[key] = true end
    end
    local pieces = Mirror.pieces(char)
    if pieces.Count >= 2 then Mirror.OwnPieces = pieces end
end
function Mirror.isYou(model, hum)
    if model.Name == lp.Name or model.Name == tostring(lp.UserId) then return true end
    -- A copy of your character made while the overlay kept it hidden (see STAGE COPIES).
    if Mirror.Unmasked[model] then return true end
    local desc = hum:FindFirstChildOfClass("HumanoidDescription")
    if desc and not desc:GetAttribute("Lyra_Description") then
        local key = Mirror.descKey(desc)
        if key ~= "" and Mirror.OwnKeys[key] then return true end
    end
    return Mirror.sameLook(model, Mirror.OwnPieces)
end
-- Whose stand-in a model is: yours, or a script user's sharing a skin through Skin sync (named after them, or wearing
-- their own avatar's pieces, read from their character as the game made it). Returns a user id or nil.
Mirror.PeerPieces = setmetatable({}, {__mode = "k"})
function Mirror.whose(model, hum)
    if Mirror.isYou(model, hum) then return lp.UserId end
    for uid in pairs(Sync.pictureUsers()) do
        local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(uid)
        if player then
            if model.Name == player.Name or model.Name == tostring(uid) or (player.DisplayName ~= "" and model.Name == player.DisplayName) then return uid end
            local character = player.Character
            if character then
                local pieces = Mirror.PeerPieces[character]
                if not pieces then pieces = Mirror.pieces(character); Mirror.PeerPieces[character] = pieces end
                if pieces.Count >= 2 and Mirror.sameLook(model, pieces) then return uid end
            end
        end
    end
    return nil
end
-- Whether a model wears an avatar's pieces (see Mirror.pieces).
function Mirror.sameLook(model, own)
    if not own then return false end
    local pieces = Mirror.pieces(model)
    local shared, accessories = 0, 0
    for key, kind in pairs(pieces.Set) do
        if own.Set[key] then
            shared = shared + 1
            if kind == "acc" then accessories = accessories + 1 end
        end
    end
    if shared >= 3 and accessories >= 2 and shared >= math.min(pieces.Count, own.Count) * 0.6 then return true end
    -- An avatar with few accessories (a hat, a shirt and pants): the model wears every piece of it and little else.
    return own.Count >= 2 and shared == own.Count and shared >= pieces.Count * 0.6
end
-- A model joined to a player's character (or held in a tool) is part of that character: resizing or moving its parts
-- would move the character too. Prison Life's guns join such a model to your character while reloading, and dressing
-- it threw the character upside down. A model joined to anything else (a lobby pedestal) is still a stand-in.
function Mirror.onPlayer(part)
    if not part then return false end
    if part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Tool") then return true end
    local model = part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
    while model do
        if Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(model) then return true end
        model = model:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
    end
    return false
end
function Mirror.joined(model)
    if model:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Tool") then return true end
    for _, part in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
        if part:IsA("BasePart") then
            local okRoot, root = pcall(function() return part.AssemblyRootPart end)
            if okRoot and root and root ~= part and not root:IsDescendantOf(model) and Mirror.onPlayer(root) then return true end
            local okJoints, joints = pcall(function() return part:GetJoints() end)
            for _, joint in ipairs(okJoints and joints or {}) do
                local a, b
                if joint:IsA("JointInstance") or joint:IsA("WeldConstraint") then a, b = joint.Part0, joint.Part1
                elseif joint:IsA("Constraint") then
                    a = joint.Attachment0 and joint.Attachment0.Parent; b = joint.Attachment1 and joint.Attachment1.Parent
                end
                for _, other in ipairs({a, b}) do
                    if other and other ~= part and not other:IsDescendantOf(model) and Mirror.onPlayer(other) then return true end
                end
            end
        end
    end
    return false
end
-- The model's Humanoid when it may be a stand-in: alive, not a player's character (nor inside one), not the copier's
-- own models, a standard R6 or R15 body. With visual-only, a copy of your body where you stand belongs to the overlay.
-- skipJoined: leave out the check of every part's joints (Mirror.check makes it once it knows whose the model is).
function Mirror.eligible(model, skipJoined)
    if not model:IsA("Model") or not model.Parent then return nil end
    local hum = model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return nil end
    local char = lp.Character
    if model == char or (char and model:IsDescendantOf(char)) then return nil end
    for _, holder in ipairs({Overlay.Folder, UI.Gui, UI.InspectOverlay, UI.InspectView}) do
        if holder and model:IsDescendantOf(holder) then return nil end
    end
    local cursor = model
    while cursor and cursor ~= game do
        if cursor:IsA("Model") and Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(cursor) then return nil end
        cursor = cursor.Parent
    end
    if not F.getTrueRigType(model) then return nil end
    if not skipJoined and Mirror.joined(model) then return nil end
    if Overlay.visualOnly() and char then
        -- "near": it may leave later (a stage copy made where you stand), so it is looked at again.
        local root = Overlay.rootOf(char)
        if root and Overlay.nearBody(model, root.Position) then return nil, "near" end
        local entry = Overlay.Active[char]
        if entry and (entry.Target == model or table.find(entry.Extra or {}, model)) then return nil, "near" end
    end
    return hum
end
function Mirror.queue(model, delay)
    if Mirror.Queued[model] then return end
    Mirror.Queued[model] = true
    task.delay(delay or 0.4, function()
        if not App.alive() then return end
        table.insert(Mirror.Queue, model)
        Mirror.run()
    end)
end
-- A model still being built (pieces arriving, joints not made yet) is looked at again: a few times while its body
-- is incomplete, once when it did not look like you yet (so games full of NPCs are not checked over and over).
function Mirror.retry(model, limit)
    local tries = (Mirror.Tries[model] or 0) + 1
    Mirror.Tries[model] = tries
    if tries <= (limit or 3) then Mirror.queue(model, 1.5) end
end
-- One model at a time, never while an avatar is being applied to your character.
function Mirror.run()
    if Mirror.Running then return end
    Mirror.Running = true
    task.spawn(function()
        while App.alive() and #Mirror.Queue > 0 do
--: YMLXO3K7GVTGMODEMRTGEMRUMNQTCNRZMQZWKMZSCE
            while App.Busy and App.alive() do task.wait(0.25) end
            local model = table.remove(Mirror.Queue, 1)
            Mirror.Queued[model] = nil
            pcall(Mirror.check, model)
        end
        Mirror.Running = false
    end)
end
Mirror.Seen = setmetatable({}, {__mode = "k"})
function Mirror.check(model)
    local known = Mirror.Known[model] ~= nil
    -- A model not known to show anyone is first asked whose it is: the closer look at every part's joints is only for
    -- models that show you or a script user (games full of NPCs spent a lot of time there).
    local hum, why = Mirror.eligible(model, not known)
    if not hum then
        if why == "near" then Mirror.retry(model, 4)
        elseif model.Parent and not Mirror.Known[model] and model:IsA("Model") and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") and not F.getTrueRigType(model) then Mirror.retry(model) end
        return
    end
    if not known then
        Mirror.Seen[model] = true
        if not Mirror.Unmasked[model] then
            local ok, copy = pcall(Overlay.unmaskCopy, model)
            if ok and copy then Mirror.Unmasked[model] = true end
        end
        local who = Mirror.whose(model, hum)
        if not who then Mirror.retry(model, 1); return end
        if Mirror.joined(model) then return end
        Mirror.Known[model] = who
        Mirror.follow(model)
        pcall(Overlay.forget, model)
        if App.tracing() then
            App.trace(string.format("Stand-in found: %s (%s, %s%s)", App.traceName(model), who == lp.UserId and "yours" or "a script user's",
                tostring(F.getTrueRigType(model)), Mirror.Unmasked[model] and ", a copy of your hidden body" or ""))
        end
    end
    Mirror.dress(model)
end
-- A script user's skin arrived, changed or went: their stand-ins follow it, and models seen before their skin
-- arrived are looked at again.
function Mirror.refreshUser(uid)
    if not App.alive() then return end
    for model, who in pairs(Mirror.Known) do if who == uid and model.Parent then Mirror.queue(model, 0) end end
    if Sync.pictureUsers()[uid] then
        for model in pairs(Mirror.Seen) do if model.Parent and not Mirror.Known[model] then Mirror.Tries[model] = nil; Mirror.queue(model, 0.2) end end
    end
end
-- A game that changes a stand-in it already showed (a new outfit in a lobby) gets it dressed again, at most three
-- times a minute.
function Mirror.follow(model)
    local connection
    connection = model.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child)
        if not App.alive() then connection:Disconnect(); return end
        if child:GetAttribute("Copier_CopiedItem") or child:GetAttribute("Lyra_VisualFor") then return end
        if not (child:IsA("Accessory") or child:IsA("Shirt") or child:IsA("Pants") or child:IsA("ShirtGraphic")) then return end
        local record = Mirror.Dressed[model]
        if not record then return end
        local now = os.clock()
        record.Changes = record.Changes or {}
        for i = #record.Changes, 1, -1 do if now - record.Changes[i] > 60 then table.remove(record.Changes, i) end end
        if #record.Changes >= 3 then return end
        table.insert(record.Changes, now)
        record.Snapshot = nil
        Mirror.queue(model, 0.8)
    end)
    RegisterConnection(connection)
end
-- Yields. The avatar model to dress stand-ins of this rig in (the one built for your character when it matches).
function Mirror.source(snapshot, rig)
    for _, row in ipairs(Mirror.Sources) do if row.Snapshot == snapshot and row.Rig == rig then return row.Model end end
    local model
    local cache = App.ModelCache
    if cache and cache.Snapshot == snapshot and cache.Rig == rig then pcall(function() model = cache.Model:Clone() end) end
    if not model then
        local decoded, desc = pcall(Codec.decode, snapshot.Data)
        if not decoded then return nil end
        local ok, made = pcall(Visual.model, snapshot.Data, desc, rig)
        pcall(function() desc:Destroy() end)
        if not ok or not made then return nil end
        model = made
    end
    table.insert(Mirror.Sources, {Snapshot = snapshot, Rig = rig, Model = model})
    while #Mirror.Sources > 6 do
        local old = table.remove(Mirror.Sources, 1)
        pcall(function() old.Model:Destroy() end)
    end
    return model
end
-- A model the physics does not move (in a menu view, or anchored as a lobby display) gets its parts placed from its
-- joints again, in the pose it has.
function Mirror.settle(model)
    if Mirror.joined(model) then return end
    local still = not model:IsDescendantOf(workspace)
    if not still then
        for _, part in ipairs(model:GetChildren()) do
            if part.Name ~= "HumanoidRootPart" and Appearance.isBody(part, model) and part.Anchored then still = true; break end
        end
    end
    if still then pcall(Rig.reachable, model, true) end
end
-- STAND-INS THE GAME HIDES OR FADES: a rhythm game keeps a copy of you on its stage and fades it in and out, a lobby
-- hides its display until you open a menu, a first-person body has no head. Dressing a stand-in made every body part
-- solid again and added items the game knows nothing about, so a hidden copy appeared as a ghost and a faded one kept
-- solid hair and hats. Now what the game gives each body part of a stand-in is kept and followed: the avatar's own
-- transparency is faded as much, and so is everything the copier put on that part (items, face, limb copies). The
-- game's values go back with the stand-in's own look.
function Mirror.fadeStop(fade)
    for _, connection in ipairs(fade and fade.Connections or {}) do connection:Disconnect() end
    if fade then fade.Connections = {} end
end
-- Before the stand-in is dressed: the transparency the game has on each body part (kept from the last time while it
-- is dressed, since the parts then carry the copier's values).
function Mirror.fadeBegin(model, record)
    local old = record and record.Fade
    Mirror.fadeStop(old)
    local fade = {Game = setmetatable({}, {__mode = "k"}), Own = setmetatable({}, {__mode = "k"}), Pending = setmetatable({}, {__mode = "k"}), Connections = {}}
    for _, part in ipairs(model:GetChildren()) do
        if Appearance.isBody(part, model) and part.Name ~= "HumanoidRootPart" then
            local value = old and old.Game[part]
            if value == nil then
                value = part:GetAttribute("Lyra_BeforeOverlay")
                if type(value) ~= "number" then value = part.Transparency end
                if isMask(value) then value = 0 end
            end
